rebuttal_or_critique: I find the continued insistence on a 'withdrawal of accommodation' stance increasingly disconnected from the current macroeconomic reality. With headline CPI at 5.02% and core inflation at 4.50%, the real policy rate is already significantly positive. Maintaining a stance of 'withdrawal of accommodation' when the repo rate is at 6.50% implies a bias toward further tightening that is not justified by the data. The GVA growth of 7.60% is robust, but we must be wary of the long policy lags; keeping an overly restrictive stance risks stifling this momentum unnecessarily. The food inflation spike of 6.56% is largely a supply-side phenomenon that monetary policy is ill-equipped to address without causing collateral damage to the broader economy. I urge the committee to acknowledge that the current policy rate is already restrictive enough to anchor expectations, and a shift to a 'neutral' stance is the appropriate signal to provide to the markets.
